# Feature: Move door — sanity check

<!-- Generated by the project-manager tool from pm.yml. Do not edit by hand; the store is the source of truth. -->

## Goal

Sanity-check candidate mechanic #79 (Move door) from Switches and Doors before it is used in real levels. Effect: opens after exactly 50 moves. Unique: opens on a move count, not a switch, key or timer. Useful: rewards planning an exact-length route. Source status in the candidate file is 'trial'.

## User Story

**As a** player

**I want** opens after exactly 50 moves.

**So that** rewards planning an exact-length route.

## High-Level Use Case

The player meets Move door for the first time in its teaching room (mech-79-move-door-room). Teaching moment: First room: the move door at the end of a route that takes about forty moves, with the counter in the HUD. A player who plays efficiently arrives in the low forties to a closed door and has to find moves to spend, which teaches that this door is measuring the length of the route rather than the player's speed or keys. The sanity check plays that room, exercises every rule below, and records a replayable session.

## Player-Facing Behavior

- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: A move counter shows in the HUD
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: The door opens permanently on your 50th move input of the attempt and stays open after it, so the puzzle is planning a route of exactly that length, not finding a key

## Edge Cases & Rules

- The door opens permanently on your 50th move input of the attempt and stays open after it, so the puzzle is planning a route of exactly that length, not finding a key
- Movement/state stays deterministic: state advances only through the pure step function with recorded t_ms; a recorded session replays to the same end state.
- Restart (R / restart) restores the room to its initial state, including this mechanic.

## UI / Feedback

- The player sees Move door's effect happen on its tile(s) exactly as the rules above describe; no hidden state.
- Any counter, inventory or HUD impact follows the rules above; if a rule needs a counter it is shown while it matters (see Open Questions).
- Failure in the teaching room returns the player to the room start / checkpoint for an immediate retry.

- Level JSON: new Test Level mech-79-move-door-room (rows + legend) implementing the teaching moment above.
- Sprites/defs: reuse existing tiles where the mechanic reuses an existing tile; add a new sprite/tile def only if this mechanic introduces a new tile (confirm in the implement task).
